rendered:
Yes, they agree. The text says a pan-genome analysis of 45 isolates[1] found 19,469 total genes, of which only 3155 (~16.2%) are core[2] genes. This analysis matches the Eduardo et al. group in Fig. 2[3]E, which shows core (>95%[4]) 3155[5], dispensable 7847[6] and unique 8467[7] genes. Added up, these come to 19,469[8], the same as the stated total. The core genes make up 1,620.5%[9] of that total, which matches the percentage in the text.

The other groups in the panel come from separate studies, which the text only describes as showing extensive genomic diversity. Their totals don't match the stated figure, and they aren't meant to. Danesh et al. adds up to 13,587[10] and Filipe et al. to 16,456[11]. The bar values come from a vision model's reading of the figure, not from printed text.

source.caption: Fig. 2. Phenotypic characteristics and genomic diversity of S. marcescens. (A) Temperature-dependent prodigiosin pigmentation phenotype; (B) distribution of the prodigiosin biosynthetic gene cluster among different biogroups; (C–D) GC content and genomic compositional characteristics; (E) pangenome composition and genomic variability; and (F) predicted host range of plasmids identified in S. marcescens. The figure summarizes the multi-level diversity of S. marcescens in phenotype, genome composition, and genetic plasticity.

source.text: Fig. 2 is a composite six-panel figure describing Serratia marcescens phenotype and genomics, organized under two headers: a purple 'Pigmented phenotype' banner covering panels A and B, and a dark blue 'Genomic features' banner covering panels C–F. (A) A schematic with a thermometer and colour gradient bar (Low to High) shows a deeply pigmented agar plate with colonies at 25–28 °C versus a pale/nonpigmented plate at ≥37 °C. (B) A table combining the classification of David et al. 2022 (phylogeny, biotype, phenotype) with the percentage of isolates from each habitat (Grimont et al. 2006) for water (107 isolates), plants and rodents (37 isolates), and hospital patients (1066 isolates); L15 biotypes A1 and A2/6 are pigmented (red text), while L13/A3, L14/A4, L9/A5/8 and L12/TCT are nonpigmented. (C) A histogram with kernel density curve of genome GC content (%) with mean μ = 59.74% marked by a dashed vertical line; the distribution is left-skewed with a major peak near 60.0%. (D) A scatter plot with marginal density plots of coding GC (%) versus intergenic GC (%) with a fitted regression line, r = 0.57, p < 0.001. (E) A grouped bar chart of pangenome gene numbers under three definitions: Eduardo et al. 2019 (core >95% = 3155, dispensable = 7847, unique = 8467), Danesh et al. 2016 (core >99% = 3372, soft core 95–99% = 342, shell 15–95% = 1526, cloud <15% = 8347), and Filipe et al. 2018 (core 100% = 2107, accessory = 7656, unique = 6693). (F) A bar chart of plasmid proportion (%) by predicted host range: genus 23.9%, family 11.3%, order 30.2%, class 2.7%, phylum 9.0%, multi-phyla 22.9%.
